nodes.label: NEMOCLAW_MODEL_BACKEND=llama
nodes.rationale: Submitting a Llama-backed agent to Meta's own challenge is a deliberate, judge-legible choice; served via a hosting provider (Together AI, Groq, AWS Bedrock) or self-hosted since Meta retired its public-preview Llama API in July 2026.

nodes.label: Notability sketch pipeline (direct display + memory plaque)
nodes.norm_label: notability sketch pipeline (direct display + memory plaque)

nodes.label: SketchScape / Shared Room product
nodes.rationale: Framed as a social/connection product (two people each contribute a meaningful object; AI infers a shared theme) rather than an object-reconstruction pipeline, to match Meta's 'Bringing People Closer Together with AI' judging criteria.

nodes.label: Unity MCP Extension for Horizon
nodes.rationale: Meta's own official Unity MCP tooling is required instead of a generic/third-party MCP server because submitting to Meta's own challenge with Meta's own official tooling is a deliberate, judge-legible choice, mirroring the Llama-backend rationale.

nodes.label: "The connection must be felt, not read" rule
nodes.norm_label: "the connection must be felt, not read" rule
nodes.rationale: The judging criterion is that AI's reasoning is visible, not that it is a caption; a floating UI text card/HUD panel would make the connection insight legible but not felt, so it must be expressed diegetically via lighting, motif, spatial audio, spoken narration, or a physically-modeled in-world text object.

nodes.label: Removed sketch->image-gen->reconstruction pipeline
nodes.rationale: Hallucinating a fake photorealistic object from a line drawing via a paid image-gen backend added a network hop and a visibly fake result for a case a direct photo upload to POST /v1/reconstructions already handles better and more honestly; removed entirely (image_gen.py, /v1/sketches, azure/hf/grok image backends) and replaced by two Notability-specific paths.

nodes.label: PIPELINE_MODE=mock
nodes.rationale: Always the default and must work offline with no GPU/AWS credentials so the judging-safe demo path never breaks; deterministic output from labels/memory text, always labelled mock in metadata.
